atoms.text: Black Americans have played an essential role in music culture in the United States. One of the most influential genres of Black American music is Soul, a style developed in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
Select here to listen to some Soul music.

Soul music brings together elements of Gospel, traditional Black Christian music, and also includes elements of Rhythm & Blues (R&B) and Jazz. It combines religious and secular lyrics to create powerful music with a message. Established during the Civil Rights Movement, Soul music spoke to a generation of young Black Americans and reflected on Black experiences in America. Many Soul songs advocated for pride, activism and unity among Black Americans. Other songs focused more on personal relationships and covered topics such as love and respect.

atoms.text: A pattern of “call and response” is often employed in Soul songs. It is like a musical conversation: the singer calls out and the backup singers or audience respond. For example, in James Brown’s “I’m Black and I’m Proud,” he calls out to the audience: “Say it loud!” In turn, they respond “I’m Black and I’m Proud!”. This pattern has its roots in West African tradition and was first practised in the US by enslaved people to communicate, express themselves and find strength while working on plantations. As Christianity gained importance among Black Americans, the “call and response” pattern became an integral part of the preaching style and Gospel sung in Black American churches. Pastors would call out a phrase or sing a line and the congregation would reply by singing back.

Soul performances are known for their emotional presentation of heartfelt lyrics paired with a rhythmic tone. Performers improvise movements and clap and shout along to catchy beats. Singers are usually accompanied by backup singers and live bands playing instruments such as the piano, guitar and drums. Soul songs also often have large brass sections, with musicians playing the saxophone, trumpet or trombone.

atoms.a: Does the bolded word have a figurative or literal meaning?

hint.text: Spoke is the simple past tense of the verb to speak. It can be used both literally and figuratively. How is it used in this context?

end.text: Soul “spoke” to the youth in a figurative sense, not literally. The music resonated with listeners and provoked an emotional response.
